opt_intro.message: A share link is a page of your edits, uploaded to a bucket you own. Whoever opens it needs Tweakpage and nothing else — no AWS account, no setup. Three steps, once.

opt_risk_title.message: These keys are readable on this machine

opt_risk_body.message: Extension storage is not a vault: anyone with access to this profile can read what you paste here, and this extension is open source. Use a key scoped to this one prefix and rotate it like any other credential. The secret itself is never sent — requests carry a signature derived from it. Shared files are readable by anyone holding the link, so keep confidential pages out of them.

opt_incomplete.message: Sharing stays off until the four AWS fields are filled.

aria_share_link.message: Upload and copy a share link

toast_share_failed.message: Upload refused. Check the bucket, the region and the key's permissions.

shared_missing.message: That link's edits are gone, or your bucket settings differ from the sender's.

marker_title.message: This page is showing local edits made with Tweakpage, not what the site serves. Click to open the editor.

tip_share_unset.message: Add your AWS details first — the gear icon above

toast_share_private.message: Uploaded, but the file is not readable, so the link would not open. Give the bucket a public-read policy for tweakpage/*, or allow the key to set object ACLs.

settings_exclusions_hint.message: The picker skips anything matching these, and everything inside it. Nothing is protected — this all runs on your copy of the page — but an edit on a chat launcher or a consent banner reproduces for nobody, and whoever receives the hand-off gets a line they cannot act on.

settings_exclusions_empty.message: Nothing is skipped. Every element on the page can be picked.

aria_exclusion_input.message: A CSS selector for a part of the page to skip

exclude_already_there.message: That rule is already in the list.

outline_shadow.message: Inside a web component — cannot be replayed

toast_share_needs_setup.message: Share links need an S3 bucket of your own. Settings is open — start there.

opt_step1_title.message: Make a bucket to keep them in

opt_step1_body.message: Any name, any region, in your own AWS account. Nothing else goes in it — Tweakpage writes only under a tweakpage/ prefix.

opt_step2_title.message: Make a key that can only write there

opt_step2_body.message: Create an IAM user with the policy below and nothing more, then take its access key. Scoped this narrowly, the worst a leaked key can do is write into that one prefix.

opt_step3_body.message: The bucket name and region from step 1, the key and secret from step 2. They stay on this computer and are never rendered into a page you edit.

opt_check_values.message: Sharing stays off until every value is one AWS will accept.

err_region.message: A region looks like ap-northeast-1, not its display name.
